compiled_state.title: As an orchestrator agent, I want a scratch CLI surface on tickets, so that I can stash large handoff payloads off-context and retrieve them by key
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Introduce `dso ticket scratch set|get|clear` subcommands and a `--include-scratch` flag on `dso ticket show`. Document the per-call-site key-namespace convention `<skill>:<step>:<purpose>` and enumerate the 5 known migrated sites so the migration story has authoritative names to consume.

**Why**: Foundation storage layer all other stories build on; walking skeleton for the epic.

**Scope**:
- IN: CLI parsing; storage at the scratch path with JSON envelope `{ts, value}`; atomic write-to-temp-then-rename (same-directory temp + fsync of temp file + parent dir); charset validation on ticket_id/key (rejects path traversal, `/`, `..`, control chars); max-byte ceiling with structured error envelope; symlink-aware path resolution; key-namespace convention documentation enumerating the 5 sites: implementation-plan:511, implementation-plan:978, implementation-plan:1238, preplanning:513, sprint:2332.
- OUT: SKILL.md migration (separate story), cleanup hooks (separate story), gitignore/reconciler isolation (separate story), measurement harness (separate story).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, `dso ticket scratch set <id> <key> <value>` writes a JSON envelope `{ts, value}` to the scratch file path using write-to-temp-then-rename, where the temp file is placed in the SAME directory as the target, fsync is called on both the temp file and the parent directory before/after rename, and a behavioral test simulating a crash between write and rename asserts no corrupt envelope is observable to a concurrent reader
  ← Satisfies: sc-1
- When this story is complete, `dso ticket scratch get <id> <key>` on hit returns `{"status":"hit","ts":<iso8601>,"value":<value>}` with exit code 0, and on miss returns `{"status":"miss","ticket_id":<id>,"key":<key>}` with exit code 0 (NOT non-zero); both shapes and exit codes are asserted by behavioral tests
  ← Satisfies: sc-1
- When this story is complete, `dso ticket scratch clear <id> [<key>]` removes a single key or the whole ticket scratch directory
  ← Satisfies: sc-1
- When this story is complete, `dso ticket show <id> --include-scratch` adds a `scratch` object to the JSON output enumerating present keys and values
  ← Satisfies: sc-1
- When this story is complete, invalid ticket_id or key characters (path traversal, slash, dot-dot, control chars, null bytes) are rejected with a structured error envelope and non-zero exit
  ← Satisfies: sc-1
- When this story is complete, writes exceeding the configured max-byte ceiling are rejected with a structured error envelope naming the limit and actual size
  ← Satisfies: sc-1
- When this story is complete, the key-namespace convention `<skill>:<step>:<purpose>` is documented in the scratch CLI reference and the 5 migrated call sites (implementation-plan:511, :978, :1238; preplanning:513; sprint:2332) have authoritative key names enumerated
  ← Satisfies: sc-1
- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic
  ← Satisfies: sc-1

## Considerations

- [Security] Input charset validation is load-bearing — fuzz path-traversal vectors (../, absolute paths, null bytes, unicode normalization).
- [Reliability] Atomic write requires temp file in the same directory as the target so rename(2) is atomic on the same filesystem; fsync discipline closes the partial-write corruption gap from the epic's Scenario Analysis.
- [Concurrency] Per-key file layout avoids contention for distinct keys; document the contract.
- [Worktree] The tickets-tracker root is a symlink in worktrees — resolve through the symlink so all sessions hit the same physical scratch directory.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
